clue.text: Censure or preach dementedly

indicators.note: acting dementedly means behaving wildly, so the letters of the two words beside it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to criticise, or to sermonise like a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke them, a close synonym of censure.

clue.text: Take off pounds of either kind

definitions.text: Take off pounds of either kind

parts.words: Take off pounds of either kind
parts.note: pounds can be units of weight shed on a diet or money taken off a price, and one verb covers both

explanation.definitionFit: To reduce is to lessen, whether weight on a dieter or the price of goods.

clue.text: Decorating with flags?

parts.note: flags suggest bunting, but here they are flagstones laid as a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Laying flagstones is covering ground with paving stones, so it is that work.

clue.text: Conservative types in Rugby, say?

parts.note: traditionalists, and also a long-established institution such as Rugby, an English public school founded in 1567

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes traditional, conservative attitudes, and literally an established ancient school such as Rugby.

clue.text: Getting better sort of home

definitions.meaning: a nursing home where patients recuperate

explanation.surface: A patient is recovering in a kind of care home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means recovering from illness and also names a home where recovering patients stay.

clue.text: Gardening accessory that's old hat

definitions.meaning: a bell-shaped glass or plastic cover put over young plants
a close-fitting bell-shaped women's hat fashionable in the 1920s

explanation.surface: A garden item is dismissed as thoroughly out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for bell names both a protective plant cover and a bell-shaped hat of the 1920s.

clue.text: An animal or bird that runs from left to right

indicators.note: the bird is placed between the letters for left and right, running from one to the other

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird that runs fast

explanation.surface: Something is either a beast or a bird racing across from one side to the other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from left to right' sets EMU between L and R; 'to' and 'or' just join.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a primate of Madagascar, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Cows, cats and hens are involved

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters of the two animals are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Farm animals and pets all get mixed up in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cows' looks like a farm noun among the cats and hens; it is the verb meaning intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to subdue or humble them, the same as to chasten.

clue.text: Coming in last after me, she gets caught

indicators.note: the two pronouns come inside the word for last

parts.note: the end is the last part
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman arriving behind me at the finish is captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming in' puts MESHE inside END; 'after' and 'gets' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmeshed means tangled in a net, so trapped or caught.

clue.text: Interest shared about a point

indicators.note: the word for shared goes round the other piece, surrounding it

parts.note: something shared out is divided
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Interest is split between parties over some point of debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is the share of profit paid to shareholders, a kind of return or interest on investment.

clue.text: Apply preservatives, a typical measure cooking lamb

parts.note: an em is a unit of measure in typography, 'typical' being read as typographical

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something else, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instructs adding preservatives and a standard amount while preparing lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'typical' is short for typographical: printers measure type width in ems. 'cooking' makes BALM.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it with preservatives against decay.

clue.text: No sane person is likely to assume it

definitions.text: No sane person is likely to assume it

parts.words: No sane person is likely to assume it
parts.note: assume here means put on a garment, the restraining jacket once used for the insane

explanation.definitionFit: This restraining canvas garment was traditionally put on violently disturbed patients.

clue.text: He finds fault in fancy nicknames

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A critic objects to elaborate pet names.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic is a sneering faultfinder who doubts the good in anything.

clue.text: Illness caused by poorly cooked Irish tart

indicators.note: a badly made dish is a mess, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone blames their sickness on a badly baked pastry from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthritis is a painful joint disease, so a type of illness.

clue.text: Fail to win a single game and get annoyed

definitions.text: Fail to win a single game
definitions.meaning: to be beaten at the one-player card game of solitaire, called Patience in Britain
to stop being tolerant and become irritated

explanation.surface: A player who never wins becomes irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: PATIENCE is the British name for solitaire, the card game played alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing patience is the idiom for becoming exasperated; literally it is being beaten at the card game.

clue.text: I clean out wound to protect from infection

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted, means the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cleans an injury to stop it festering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury, but read it as the past of wind: twisted, which signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to vaccinate, giving protection against a disease.

clue.text: Heading for the frozen wastes — or stuck in them

definitions.meaning: bound for the ice, travelling towards it
trapped fast in ice, as a ship can be

explanation.surface: An expedition sets out for the polar ice, or is trapped in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word normally means held fast by ice, but read literally it means bound for the ice.

clue.text: Providing the Lord's judgment?

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground, where decisions are given by the official in white coat

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is a famous cricket ground in London, not a reference to God.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket official gives decisions on the field, so supplying judgments at Lord's is this activity.

clue.text: Difficulty produced by aggravation of illness

definitions.meaning: a snag or problem making things harder
in medicine, a secondary condition that worsens an existing disease

explanation.surface: Some problem arises because a sickness has got worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a general snag and, medically, a secondary condition worsening a disease.

clue.text: About to take successful action to recover money

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a coup is a brilliant, successful stroke

explanation.surface: Someone is about to make a smart move to get their money back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to win back or regain money spent.

clue.text: Fool about to declare in tests

indicators.note: the word for fool goes around the word for declare

parts.note: an ass is a fool
to say is to declare

explanation.surface: An idiot is on the point of announcing something during examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay a metal is to test its purity, so assays are tests.

clue.text: Copper was impressed with the old Royal Yacht

definitions.meaning: the seated female figure stamped on old British copper pennies
the name of the British monarch's yacht, decommissioned in 1997

explanation.surface: A policeman was dazzled by the former royal vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal of old British pennies, which bore the figure of Britannia.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure personifying Britain was struck on copper pennies, and the same name was given to the royal yacht.

clue.text: A place to see pigeons flying

parts.note: a loft is where pigeons are kept by fanciers

explanation.surface: A spot where pigeons can be seen on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means high up in the air, so airborne or flying.

clue.text: Drug addicts may be found out in devious ruses

indicators.note: devious means twisting and indirect, so the letters of the next word take a new order

explanation.surface: Addicts are said to be uncovered through cunning tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug users are people who take drugs, so addicts in this context.

clue.text: Agreement to give son in marriage

indicators.note: the letter for son is placed within the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union of two people
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent consents to hand over a son at a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in unison is to act in complete agreement, together.

clue.text: Musical state

definitions.meaning: the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1943
a US state in the south-central plains

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to an American state and to a famous stage musical set there.

clue.text: Understand it's including one's fingers and toes

parts.note: to dig something is slang for understanding or appreciating it
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone appreciates a joke that involves counting on their extremities.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits is the anatomical word for fingers and toes.

clue.text: Takes a shot at decoys

parts.note: taken as written
to decoy is to lure, so decoys means tempts

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at the wooden birds used to lure game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoys' looks like a noun, the wooden ducks shot at, but it is a verb meaning lures.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a shot at something is idiom for trying it, which is what attempts means.
